invariants: Nothing leaves an installation for an integration that is not enabled. Handlers for disabled integrations answer 403 integration_disabled.
With EVER_CONNECT_ENABLED unset or false, the Ever Connect module is not loaded and the installation makes no calls to any Ever Platform host.
Only the fields listed under scope may move, and only in the listed form and at the listed frequency.
An installation operator can deny any integration for every tenant with EVER_CONNECT_INTEGRATIONS_DENY=<key,...>. The state becomes denied_by_policy, which tenant administrators cannot override.

Consent is granted by an organization owner or admin in app.ever.co. Where a product later offers its own consent dialog, it will ask for a fresh Ever ID sign-in and record the same consent. Discoverability and the installation address are enabled in app.ever.co only. Each consent is recorded, can be revoked at any time, and every change is logged.

Integrations that act for the whole installation (instance_url, stats_link, ever_id_login, webhooks) can be enabled only by the organization that owns the installation's connection, and they start only after the installation's operator also accepts them on the installation, on multi-tenant servers too.
No per-record business data (invoices, amounts, customer lists, documents) is sent to Ever Platform by any integration in this catalog.
Anonymous usage statistics (ever.stats.v1) are not an integration. They follow their own published allow-list and are switched off with EVER_STATS_ENABLED=false.

integrations.name: Installation address
integrations.description: Shows the public address of this installation to its own organization in app.ever.co, and on the public profile if the owner turns that section on.

scope.purpose: Link to this installation from the organization's account pages
scope.retention: Kept while the integration is enabled. Deleted when it is turned off or the installation disconnects.

integrations.name: Link usage statistics to this organization
integrations.description: Connects the anonymous statistics identity of this self-hosted installation to your organization, so you can see your installation's latest statistics report in app.ever.co. Without this link, statistics stay anonymous. It is never offered on Ever Cloud, where one installation serves many organizations.
integrations.revoke_effect: The link is cleared. Later statistics reports are anonymous again.

scope.purpose: Match the installation's anonymous statistics identity to the connected installation
scope.retention: Kept while the integration is enabled.

scope.purpose: The public half of the separate statistics key, so the link can be checked against the key that signs the reports
scope.retention: Kept while the integration is enabled.

scope.purpose: Signature made with the statistics key, proving that the connected installation holds it
scope.retention: Kept while the integration is enabled.

integrations.name: Sign in with Ever ID
integrations.description: Adds Ever ID as an extra sign-in option in this installation. Existing sign-in methods keep working unchanged.
integrations.revoke_effect: Ever refuses this installation's Ever ID requests at once (its client, its users' links, lookups). The identity provider stops signing people in through the installation's client once Ever deactivates it, shortly after and retried until it succeeds; until then a sign-in still completes, and for about a minute after the revocation (a cache) it may still carry this installation's organization data from Ever, then none. The client is never deleted: enabling the integration again reuses it with a new secret. Its users' links are marked unlinked, so deletion and export requests no longer reach it. Sign-in tokens already issued stay valid until they expire. Local accounts and sessions are not affected.
integrations.notes: Ever Teams signs in through its Gauzy API, so it is covered by the gauzy row.

scope.purpose: Register the sign-in callback address of this installation
scope.retention: Kept with the installation's record after the integration ends, so enabling it again reuses the client.

scope.purpose: Register the sign-out address; Ever ID also sends its sign-out notices there (they carry the Ever ID and a session id)
scope.retention: Kept with the installation's record after the integration ends, so enabling it again reuses the client.

scope.retention: Kept while linked. When the user unlinks or the integration ends, the link is marked unlinked and kept, unused, until the person's Ever account is deleted.

scope.purpose: This installation's answer to a person's deletion or export request: deleted, anonymised, exported, no account, kept under a legal obligation (with its legal basis, up to 200 characters), forwarded to another controller (its kind and when it was told), or failed (with a reason code)

scope.purpose: Client identifier for this installation
scope.retention: Kept with the installation's record after the integration ends, so enabling it again reuses the client.

scope.purpose: Client secret, handed over once and stored encrypted by the installation
scope.retention: Ever holds it encrypted only until the installation first reads it, then erases its copy.

scope.purpose: At each sign-in through this installation, Ever ID gives it the person's Ever ID, e-mail address (and whether it is verified), name, language, Ever person id, the kind of Ever ID (for a company-managed Ever ID, the id of the managing organization, even when that organization is not linked to this installation), and the organizations linked to this installation with the person's role, tenant and tier
scope.retention: Not kept by Ever beyond the sign-in; the installation keeps what it needs.

scope.purpose: When the installation asks about one of its linked users: their Ever person id, name and account status, the kind of Ever ID (for a company-managed Ever ID, the id of the managing organization, even when it is not linked to this installation), and for the organizations linked to this installation their id, handle, the person's role, tier and links (never an e-mail address)
scope.retention: The answer is not kept. Ever keeps the person's organization context (ids, roles, links) in its sign-in cache, refreshed at each sign-in or lookup and deleted with the person's Ever account.

scope.purpose: A linked person's deletion or export request, naming the person by Ever's person id and by a hash of each Ever ID this installation linked, with the request id and the date to answer by
scope.retention: Kept in the installation's event feed for the event retention period (90 days by default); the hashes stay with the person's deletion record.

integrations.name: Check contacts on Ever Platform

The values themselves never leave the installation.
integrations.revoke_effect: The button is hidden and cached results are purged.
integrations.notes: Automatic checking when a contact is opened is a separate setting. It is off by default and is part of this scope text.

integrations.name: Usage reporting
integrations.description: Sends daily counts of a plan's metered quantities (for example active employees or seats) for plans that are priced by usage. On Ever Cloud it will start on under the Ever Cloud terms once cloud plans are billed on these counts (for example per employee for Ever Gauzy and Ever Teams, on the latest successful count); until then it stays off. A self-hosted installation sends nothing unless an administrator turns it on.
integrations.notes: Ever Cloud: will start on under the Ever Cloud terms once per-usage cloud billing is available (for example Ever Gauzy and Ever Teams per-employee plans; a missed count never raises the bill above the last known number); off until then. Self-hosted: off unless an administrator consents.

integrations.name: Maintenance operations
integrations.description: Lets an owner or admin ask this self-hosted installation, from app.ever.co, to run a maintenance operation: an update, a backup, a restore check or a health report. Requests reach the installation through its own outbound connection; the operator also turns the feature on locally and sets when and what may run. Backups stay in your own storage, and Ever Platform sees only each operation's status and size. Ever never connects in.
integrations.revoke_effect: Queued operations are cancelled and nothing further runs.
integrations.notes: Ever already operates its cloud installations, so this is offered on self-hosted installations only. It becomes active per product once that product can run the operations. Ever Teams is covered by its Ever Gauzy server.
